getRadioChannel.description: The function is used to retrieve the ID of the current radio channel.

getRadioChannelName.description: This function gets the given radio channel name.

getSFXStatus.description: In case of these invalid audio files, this function returns _false_. This function checks if a big sound container is available to use or not.

getSoundBPM.description: This function gets the beats per minute of a specific [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") element.

getSoundBufferLength.description: This function gets the buffer playback length of the specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound"). Works only with streams.

getSoundEffectParameters.description: This function gets the parameters of a [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") effect.

getSoundEffects.description: Returns the states of all effects of a sound.

getSoundFFTData.description: This function gets the fast fourier transform data for an audio stream which is a table of floats representing the current audio frame. This allows things like visualisations. A fast fourier transform generates a table of all the frequencies of the current audio frame which starts at the bass end of the spectrum to mids to highs in that order. Should you have any problems there is an example resource located on the resources repository: [Visualiser](https://github.com/multitheftauto/mtasa-resources/tree/master/%5Bgameplay%5D/visualiser) Just type "startmusic mystreamurl" in your console and it will play on the cinema billboard near A51. If the element is a player, this function will use the players voice.

getSoundLength.description: This function is used to return the playback length of the specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") element. If the element is a player, this function will use the players voice.

getSoundLevelData.description: This function gets the left/right level from a [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element"). If the element is a player, this function will use the players voice.

getSoundMaxDistance.description: Gets a custom [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") max distance at which the sound stops.

getSoundMetaTags.description: Used to get the meta tags attached to a sound. These provide information about the sound, for instance the title or the artist.

getSoundMinDistance.description: Gets a custom [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") Minimum distance at which the sound stops getting louder.

getSoundPan.description: This function is used to get the pan level of the specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") element.

getSoundPosition.description: This function is used to return the current seek position of the specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") element. If the element is a player, this function will use the players voice.

getSoundProperties.description: This function gets the properties of a specific [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound").

getSoundSpeed.description: This function is used to return the playback speed of the specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element").

getSoundVolume.description: This function is used to return the volume level of the specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element"). If the element is a [player](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Player "Player"), this function will use the players voice.

getSoundWaveData.description: This function gets the wave form data for an audio stream which is a table of floats representing the current audio frame as a wave. This allows things like visualisations. If the element is a player, this function will use the players voice.

isSoundLooped.description: This function is used to return the current loop state of the [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element").

isSoundPanningEnabled.description: This function checks whether panning is enabled in a [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element") or not.

isSoundPaused.description: This function is used to return the current pause state of the specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element"). If the element is a [player](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Player "Player"), this function will use the players voice.

playSFX3D.description: This function plays a sound in the GTA world from GTA's big sound containers. In case of these invalid audio files, this function returns _false_. It also returns _false_ when trying to play a track deleted in the recent GTA: SA Steam patches (and if the client is using a Steam GTA: SA copy).

playSFX.description: This function plays a sound from GTA's big sound containers. In case of these invalid audio files, this function returns _false_. It also returns _false_ when trying to play a track deleted in the recent GTA: SA Steam patches (and if the client is using a Steam GTA: SA copy).

playSound3D.description: Creates a [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element") in the GTA world and plays it immediately after creation for the local player. [setElementPosition](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/SetElementPosition "SetElementPosition") can be used to move the [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") element around after it has been created. Remember to use [setElementDimension](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/SetElementDimension "SetElementDimension") after creating the sound to play it outside of dimension 0. Added the feature of playing WebM files.

playSound.description: Creates a [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element") and plays it immediately after creation for the local player. Added the feature of playing WebM files.

setRadioChannel.description: This function sets the heard radio channel, even while not in a vehicle.

setSoundEffectEnabled.description: Used to enable or disable specific [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") effects. Use a [player](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Player "Player") element to control a players voice with this function.

setSoundEffectParameter.description: This function sets the parameter of a [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") effect.

setSoundLooped.description: This function is used to change the loop state of the [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element").

setSoundMaxDistance.description: Sets a custom [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") max distance at which the sound stops.

setSoundMinDistance.description: Sets a custom [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") Minimum distance at which the sound stops getting louder.

setSoundPan.description: This function is used to change the pan level of the specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") element.

setSoundPanningEnabled.description: This function toggles the panning of a sound (hearing it closer to the left or right side of the speakers due to the camera position). By default a sound has its panning enabled.

setSoundPaused.description: This function is used to either pause or unpause the playback of the specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element"). Use a player element to control a players voice with this function.

setSoundPosition.description: This function is used to change the seek position of the specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") element. Use a player element to control a players voice with this function.

setSoundProperties.description: This function edits the properties of a specific [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound").

setSoundSpeed.description: This function can be used to change the playback speed of the specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element").

setSoundVolume.description: This function is used to change the volume level of the specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element"). Use a player element to control a players voice with this function.

stopSound.description: Stops the sound playback for specified [sound](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Sound "Sound") [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element"). The sound element is also destroyed.

playSoundFrontEnd.description: This function plays a frontend sound for the specified player.

canBrowserNavigateBack.description: This function checks if the browser can return to the previous page.

canBrowserNavigateForward.description: This function checks if the browser can go to the next page.

createBrowser.description: This function creates a new web [browser](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Browser "Element/Browser") element.

executeBrowserJavascript.description: This function executes a Javascript string to the specified [browser](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Browser "Element/Browser"). Works only with local browsers.

focusBrowser.description: This function will attempt to focus the [browser](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Browser "Element/Browser") or unfocus all browsers. The browser that is focused will retrieve keyboard input.

getBrowserProperty.description: This function gets a given property of a specified browser.

getBrowserSettings.description: This function returns a table containing the browser settings.

getBrowserSource.description: This function can be used to retrieve the source code of a website (asynchronously). The size of the source code is limited to 2 MiB (remaining bytes are cut).

getBrowserTitle.description: This function returns the title of the passed [browser](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Browser "Element/Browser").

getBrowserURL.description: This function returns the URL of the specified [browser](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Browser "Element/Browser").

injectBrowserMouseDown.description: This function injects a mouse click (state: down).

injectBrowserMouseMove.description: This function injects a mouse movement.

injectBrowserMouseUp.description: This function injects a mouse click (state: up).

injectBrowserMouseWheel.description: This function injects mouse wheel events.

isBrowserDomainBlocked.description: This function checks if the specified URL is blocked from being loaded.

isBrowserFocused.description: This function checks if a browser is focused.

isBrowserLoading.description: This function checks if a browser is currently loading a website.

isBrowserRenderingPaused.description: This function gets the rendering state of a [browser](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Browser "Browser") [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element").

loadBrowserURL.description: This function loads the specified URL.

navigateBrowserBack.description: Returns the browser to the previous page.

navigateBrowserForward.description: This function takes the browser to the next page.

reloadBrowserPage.description: This function reloads the current browser's page.

requestBrowserDomains.description: This function opens a request window in order to accept the requested remote URLs.

resizeBrowser.description: Allows resizing of CEF browsers at runtime.

setBrowserAjaxHandler.description: This function provides a requestable ajax resource for Lua/Javascript communication for a [browser](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Browser "Element/Browser").

setBrowserProperty.description: This function sets a given property of a specified browser.

setBrowserRenderingPaused.description: This function sets the rendering state of a browser.

setBrowserVolume.description: This function sets either a specific [browser](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Browser "Element/Browser")'s volume, or the overall volume for browsers.

toggleBrowserDevTools.description: This function toggles the visibility of the developer tools pane.

isBrowserGPUEnabled.description: **Note**: this is a global setting, not specific to any browser instance and can only be changed by the client.

getCamera.description: This function returns an [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element") that corresponds to the game camera

getCameraClip.description: This function checks if the camera will "collide" with any objects or vehicles in its way. Read more about this [here](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/SetCameraClip "SetCameraClip").

getCameraFieldOfView.description: This function returns the field of view of the _dynamic camera_ as set by [setCameraFieldOfView](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/SetCameraFieldOfView "SetCameraFieldOfView").

getCameraGoggleEffect.description: This function returns what goggle effect is currently affecting the camera.

getCameraViewMode.description: This function allows you to get the active camera view modes. This indicates at what distance the camera will follow the player or vehicle.

setCameraClip.description: This function sets if the camera will "collide" with any objects or vehicles in its way. This means that if object clip is enabled an object is in the way of where the camera actually wants to be, the camera will try to be in front of it. This function can disable that.

setCameraFieldOfView.description: This function sets the field of view of the _dynamic camera_ - this is the field of view of the _non-fixed camera_ - yes, the camera that the user can control whilst on foot or in a vehicle. The higher the field of view angle, the more you will be able to see to your sides.

setCameraGoggleEffect.description: This function allows you to set the camera's current goggle effect. This means you can activate nightvision or infrared effects by script

setCameraDrunkLevel.description: Drunk effect is a wavy motion of the camera depicting the player being drunk. This function used to be called [setCameraShakeLevel](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/SetCameraShakeLevel "SetCameraShakeLevel") which has since been deprecated.

setCameraViewMode.description: This function allows you to set the camera view modes. This indicates at what distance the camera will follow the player or vehicle.

shakeCamera.description: This function allows you to trigger camera shake effect (just like explosion does).

resetShakeCamera.description: This function cancels the chaking effect caused by **shakeCamera**

fadeCamera.description: This function will fade a player's camera to a color or back to normal over a specified time period. This will also affect the sound volume for the player (50% faded = 50% volume, full fade = no sound). For clientside scripts you can perform 2 fade ins or fade outs in a row, but for serverside scripts you must use one then the other.

getCameraInterior.description: Returns the interior of the local camera (independent of the interior of the local player).

float.description: This function returns the position of the specified marker's target, the position it points to. This only works for checkpoint markers and ring markers. For checkpoints it returns the position the arrow is pointing to, for ring markers it returns the position the ring is facing. You can set this target with [setMarkerTarget](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/SetMarkerTarget "SetMarkerTarget").

getCameraTarget.description: This function returns an [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element") that corresponds to the current target of the specified player's camera (i.e. what it is following).

setCameraInterior.description: Sets the interior of the local camera. Only the interior of the camera is changed, the local player stays in the interior he was in.

setCameraMatrix.description: This function sets the camera's position and direction. The first three arguments are the point at which the camera lies, the last three are the point the camera faces (or the point it "looks at").

setCameraTarget.description: This function allows you to set a player's camera to follow other elements instead. Currently supported element type is:

getCursorAlpha.description: This function is used to get the client's cursor alpha (transparency).

getCursorPosition.description: This function gets the current position of the mouse cursor. Note that for performance reasons, the world position returned is always 300 units away. If you want the exact world point (similar to [onClientClick](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnClientClick "OnClientClick")), use [processLineOfSight](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/ProcessLineOfSight "ProcessLineOfSight") between the camera position and the worldX/Y/Z result of this function. (See example below)

setCursorAlpha.description: This function is used to change alpha (transparency) from the client's cursor.

setCursorPosition.description: This function sets the current position of the mouse cursor.

showCursor.description: This function is used to show or hide a [player](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Player "Player")'s cursor.

dxConvertPixels.description: This function converts [pixels](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Texture_pixels "Texture pixels") from one format to another.

dxCreateFont.description: This function creates a [DX font](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DX_font "DX font") element that can be used in [dxDrawText](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DxDrawText "DxDrawText"). Successful font creation is not guaranteed, and may fail due to hardware or memory limitations. To see if creation is likely to fail, use [dxGetStatus](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DxGetStatus "DxGetStatus"). (When **VideoMemoryFreeForMTA** is zero, failure _is_ guaranteed.)

dxCreateRenderTarget.description: This function creates a render target element, which is a special type of [texture](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Texture "Texture") that can be drawn on with the dx functions. Successful render target creation is not guaranteed, and may fail due to hardware or memory limitations. To see if creation is likely to fail, use [dxGetStatus](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DxGetStatus "DxGetStatus"). (When **VideoMemoryFreeForMTA** is zero, failure _is_ guaranteed.)

dxCreateScreenSource.description: This function creates a screen source, which is a special type of [texture](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Texture "Texture") that contains the screen as rendered by GTA Note that successful screen source creation is not guaranteed, and may fail due to hardware or memory limitations. You should always check to see if this function has returned false.

dxCreateShader.description: This function creates a [shader](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Shader "Shader") element that can be used in the dxDraw functions. Successful shader creation is not guaranteed unless the [Effect File](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Shader "Shader") contains a fallback technique which will work on every existing PC.

dxCreateTexture.description: This function creates a [texture](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Texture "Texture") element that can be used in the dxDraw functions. It is possible to use dxCreateTexture to load cubemaps and volume textures, but these will only be useable as inputs for a shader. The Microsoft utility [DxTex](http://nightly.mtasa.com/files/shaders/DxTex.zip) can view and change cubemaps and volume textures. DxTex can also convert standard textures into DXT1/3/5 compressed .dds which should reduce file sizes.

dxDrawCircle.description: This function draws a circle shape on the screen - rendered for **one** frame. This should be used in conjunction with [onClientRender](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnClientRender "OnClientRender") in order to be display continuously.

dxDrawImage.description:
Draws an image on the screen for a single frame. In order for the image to stay visible continuously, you need to call this function with the same parameters on each frame update (see [onClientRender](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnClientRender "OnClientRender")).  
Image files should ideally have dimensions that are a power of two, to prevent possible blurring.  
**Power of two: 2px, 4px, 8px, 16px, 32px, 64px, 128px, 256px, 512px, 1024px...**

dxDrawImageSection.description:
Differing from [dxDrawImage](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DxDrawImage "DxDrawImage"), this function only draws a part of an image on the screen for a single frame. In order for the image to stay visible continuously, you need to call this function with the same parameters on each frame update (see [onClientRender](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnClientRender "OnClientRender")). Image files should ideally have dimensions that are a power of two, to prevent possible blurring.  
**Power of two: 2px, 4px, 8px, 16px, 32px, 64px, 128px, 256px, 512px, 1024px...**

dxDrawLine.description: This function draws a 2D line across the screen - rendered for **one** frame. This should be used in conjunction with [onClientRender](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnClientRender "OnClientRender") in order to display continuously.

dxDrawLine3D.description: This function draws a 3D line between two points in the 3D world - rendered for **one** frame. This should be used in conjunction with [onClientRender](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnClientRender "OnClientRender") in order to display continuously.

dxDrawMaterialLine3D.description: This function draws a textured 3D line between two points in the 3D world - rendered for one frame. This should be used in conjunction with [onClientPreRender](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnClientPreRender "OnClientPreRender") in order to display continuously. The 3D line with a large width value effectively becomes a rectangle, so it it possible to construct basic shapes such as boxes with several large width lines and the appropriate values for 'faceToward'. 3D lines are drawn at a particular place in the [game processing order](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Game_Processing_Order "Game Processing Order"), so use [onClientPreRender](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnClientPreRender "OnClientPreRender") for drawing if you are attaching them to world elements.

dxDrawMaterialPrimitive.description: This function draws a 2D primitive shape with material applied to it across the screen - rendered for one frame. This should be used in conjunction with [onClientRender](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnClientRender "OnClientRender") in order to display continuously. If image file is used, it should ideally have dimensions that are a power of two, to prevent possible blurring. Power of two: 2px, 4px, 8px, 16px, 32px, 64px, 128px, 256px, 512px, 1024px...

dxDrawMaterialPrimitive3D.description: This function draws a 3D primitive shape with material applied to it in the 3D world - rendered for one frame. This should be used in conjunction with [onClientRender](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnClientRender "OnClientRender") in order to display continuously. If image file is used, it should ideally have dimensions that are a power of two, to prevent possible blurring. Power of two: 2px, 4px, 8px, 16px, 32px, 64px, 128px, 256px, 512px, 1024px...

dxDrawMaterialSectionLine3D.description: This function draws a textured 3D line between two points in the 3D world - rendered for one frame. This should be used in conjunction with [onClientPreRender](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnClientPreRender "OnClientPreRender") in order to display continuously. The 3D line with a large width value effectively becomes a rectangle, so it it possible to construct basic shapes such as boxes with several large width lines and the appropriate values for 'faceToward'.

dxDrawModel3D.description: This function draws a 3D model - rendered for **one** frame. Drawn models are indistinguishable from this one created by [createObject](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/CreateObject "CreateObject") function. This should be used in conjunction with [onClientRender](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnClientRender "OnClientRender") or [onClientPreRender](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnClientPreRender "OnClientPreRender") in order to display continuously. Note that a model must be loaded at the time this function is called. A model can be loaded and unloaded with the help of [engineStreamingRequestModel](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/EngineStreamingRequestModel "EngineStreamingRequestModel") and [engineStreamingReleaseModel](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/EngineStreamingReleaseModel "EngineStreamingReleaseModel") functions.

dxDrawPrimitive.description: This function draws a 2D primitive shape across the screen - rendered for one frame. This should be used in conjunction with [onClientRender](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnClientRender "OnClientRender") in order to display continuously.

dxDrawPrimitive3D.description: This function draws a 3D primitive in the 3D world - rendered for **one** frame. This should be used in conjunction with [onClientRender](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnClientRender "OnClientRender") in order to display continuously.

dxDrawRectangle.description: This function draws a 2D rectangle across the screen - rendered for **one** frame. This should be used in conjunction with [onClientRender](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnClientRender "OnClientRender") in order to display continuously.

dxDrawText.description: Draws a string of text on the screen for one frame. In order for the text to stay visible continuously, you need to call this function with the same parameters on each frame update (see [onClientRender](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnClientRender "OnClientRender")).

dxDrawWiredSphere.description: This function drawn same sphere as /showcol. It provides 4 levels of iterations which mean density of sphere. Adjust radius to iterations to get optimum density of mesh. About 50 spheres with iterations = 4 can cause fps drop.

dxGetBlendMode.description: This function returns the current blend mode for the dxDraw functions. The blend mode is set using [dxSetBlendMode](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DxSetBlendMode "DxSetBlendMode")

dxGetFontHeight.description: This function retrieves the theoretical height of a certain piece of text, if it were to be drawn using [dxDrawText](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DxDrawText "DxDrawText").

material.description: This gets the dimensions of the supplied [material](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Material "Material") element.

dxGetPixelColor.description: This function gets the color of a single pixel from [pixels](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Texture_pixels "Texture pixels") contained in a string. It only works with '**plain'** format pixels.

dxGetPixelsSize.description: This function gets the dimensions of [pixels](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Texture_pixels "Texture pixels") contained in a string. It works with all pixel formats.

dxGetPixelsFormat.description: This function returns the format of [pixels](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Texture_pixels "Texture pixels") contained in a string.

dxGetStatus.description: This function gets information about various internal datum.

dxGetTextSize.description: This function retrieves the theoretical width and height (in pixels) of a certain piece of text, if it were to be drawn using [dxDrawText](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DxDrawText "DxDrawText"). **NOTE:** This function already takes the client's screen resolution into account.

dxGetTextWidth.description: This function retrieves the theoretical width (in pixels) of a certain piece of text, if it were to be drawn using [dxDrawText](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DxDrawText "DxDrawText"). **NOTE:** This function already takes the client's screen resolution into account.

dxGetTexturePixels.description: This function fetches the [pixels](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Texture_pixels "Texture pixels") from a [texture](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Texture "Texture") element. It can be used with a standard texture, render target or screen source.

dxIsAspectRatioAdjustmentEnabled.description: This function gets the current aspect ratio set by [dxSetAspectRatioAdjustmentEnabled](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DxSetAspectRatioAdjustmentEnabled "DxSetAspectRatioAdjustmentEnabled").

dxSetAspectRatioAdjustmentEnabled.description: This function allows for the positioning of dxDraw calls to be automatically adjusted according to the client's aspect ratio setting. This lasts for a single execution of an event handler for one of the following events: [onClientRender](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnClientRender "OnClientRender"), [onClientPreRender](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnClientPreRender "OnClientPreRender") and [onClientHUDRender](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnClientHUDRender "OnClientHUDRender"). So the function has to be called every frame, just like dxDraws. This is particularly useful for draws that must align with the GTA HUD, for which the sizing and positioning can vary for different aspect ratios.

dxSetBlendMode.description: This function sets the current blend mode for the dxDraw functions. Changing the blend mode can increase the quality when drawing text or certain other images to a render target. As a general guide use **modulate\_add** when drawing text to a render target, and **add** when drawing the render target to the screen. Don't forget to restore the default **blend** at the end - See the example below.

dxSetPixelColor.description: This function sets the color of a single pixel for [pixels](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Texture_pixels "Texture pixels") contained in a string. It only works with '**plain'** format pixels.

dxSetRenderTarget.description: This function changes the drawing destination for the dx functions. It can be used to select a previously created render target, or if called with no arguments, restore drawing directly to the screen.

dxSetShaderValue.description: This sets a named parameter for a [shader](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Shader "Shader") element

dxSetShaderTessellation.description: This function sets the amount of geometric sub-division to use when drawing a [shader](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Shader "Shader") element with [dxDrawImage](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DxDrawImage "DxDrawImage"). Using tessellation allows a shader to manipulate the shape of the rendered image at each sub-division boundary.

dxSetShaderTransform.description: This function applies a 3D transformation to a [shader](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Shader "Shader") element when it is drawn with [dxDrawImage](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DxDrawImage "DxDrawImage").

dxSetTestMode.description: This function is used for testing scripts written using [guiCreateFont](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/GuiCreateFont "GuiCreateFont"), [dxCreateFont](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DxCreateFont "DxCreateFont"), [dxCreateShader](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DxCreateShader "DxCreateShader") and [dxCreateRenderTarget](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DxCreateRenderTarget "DxCreateRenderTarget"). Each one of the 3 test modes should be used in turn to help highlight any potential problems.

dxSetTextureEdge.description: This functions allows you to change the edge handling after creating the texture. [![TextureEdges.jpg](/images/thumb/0/08/TextureEdges.jpg/600px-TextureEdges.jpg)](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/File:TextureEdges.jpg)

dxSetTexturePixels.description: This function sets the [pixels](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Texture_pixels "Texture pixels") of a [texture](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Texture "Texture") element. It can be used with a standard texture, render target or screen source. Only '**plain'** format pixels please.

dxUpdateScreenSource.description: This function updates the contents of a screen source [texture](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Texture "Texture") with the screen output from GTA

fxAddBlood.description: Creates a blood splatter particle effect.

fxAddBulletImpact.description: Creates a bullet impact particle effect, consisting of a small smoke cloud and a number of sparks.

fxAddBulletSplash.description: This function creates a bullet splash particle effect, normally created when shooting into water.

fxAddDebris.description: Creates a debris particle effect (e.g. bits that fly off a car when ramming a wall).

fxAddFootSplash.description: This function creates a foot splash particle effect, normally created when walking into water.

fxAddGlass.description: This function creates a glass particle effect.

fxAddGunshot.description: This function creates a gunshot particle effect.

fxAddPunchImpact.description: Creates a punch impact particle effect (a small dust cloud).

fxAddSparks.description: Creates a number of sparks originating from a point or along a line.

fxAddTankFire.description: This function creates a tank firing particle effect.

fxAddTyreBurst.description: Creates a tyre burst particle effect (a small white smoke puff).

fxAddWaterHydrant.description: This function creates a water hydrant particle effect.

fxAddWaterSplash.description: This function creates a water splash particle effect.

fxAddWood.description: Creates a wood splinter particle effect.

getEffectDensity.description: This function gets the density of certain [effect](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Effect "Effect").

getEffectSpeed.description: This function gets the speed of a specified [effect](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Effect "Effect").

setEffectDensity.description: This function sets the density of a specified [effect](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Effect "Effect"). The limit is 1 for Low, 1.5 for Medium, and 2 for High/Very high.

setEffectSpeed.description: This function sets the speed of a specified [effect](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Effect "Effect").

getElementBoneMatrix.description: This function returns the transformation matrix of a specific bone. Currently the [Player](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Player "Element/Player") and [Ped](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Ped "Element/Ped") element types are accepted.

getElementBonePosition.description: Returns the 3D world coordinates of a specific bone of a given [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element"). Currently the [Player](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Player "Element/Player") and [Ped](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Ped "Element/Ped") element types are accepted.

getElementBoneRotation.description: Returns the orientation of a specific bone relative to the [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element"). Currently the [Player](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Player "Element/Player") and [Ped](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Ped "Element/Ped") element types are accepted.

getElementBoneQuaternion.description:
This function retrieves how a particular bone rotates in relation to the element.  
The use of [quaternions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quaternion) are more effective and do not generate issues like gimbal lock that might arise with [Euler angles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_angles), so they are a preferable choice for rotation.

getElementBoundingBox.description: This function returns the minimum and maximum coordinates of an element's bounding box. It should be noted that the values returned are relative to the position of the element, and as such if you wish to get world coordinates for drawing, etc., you should retrieve the position of the element and add the returned values onto that.

getElementDistanceFromCentreOfMassToBase.description: This function is used to retrieve the distance between a [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element")'s centre of mass to the base of the model. This can be used to calculate the position the [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element") has to be set to, to have it on ground level.

getElementLighting.description: This function returns the lighting value for the specified [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element"). This can be a [player](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Player "Player"), [ped](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Ped "Ped"), [vehicle](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Vehicle "Vehicle"), [object](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Object "Object").

getElementRadius.description: This function gets the radius of an [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element"). Normally, sphere or circle-shaped elements tend to return a more accurate and expected radius than others with another shapes.

isElementCollidableWith.description:
This function can be used to check whether specified element is collidable with another element.  
**Note:** You can only use this function with the element types listed below.

isElementLocal.description: This function checks whether a clientside [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element") is local to the client (doesn't exist in the server) or not.

isElementOnScreen.description: This function will check if an element is on the screen. Elements behind objects but still in the camera view count as being on screen. This function is particularly useful for detecting if dynamic objects are in "destroyed" state. Destroyed objects will return false.

isElementStreamable.description: This function checks whether an [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element") is streamable as set by [setElementStreamable](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/SetElementStreamable "SetElementStreamable") or not.

isElementStreamedIn.description: This function checks whether an [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element") is currently streamed in (not virtualized) and are actual GTA objects in the world. You can force an element to be streamed in using [setElementStreamable](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/SetElementStreamable "SetElementStreamable").

isElementSyncer.description: This function checks whether an [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element") is synced by the local player or not. Accepted elements are [peds](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Ped "Ped") and [vehicles](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Vehicle "Vehicle").

isElementWaitingForGroundToLoad.description: This function checks whether MTA has frozen an element because it is above map objects which are still loading or not.

setElementBoneMatrix.description: This function sets the transformation matrix of a specific bone. Currently the [Player](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Player "Element/Player") and [Ped](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Ped "Element/Ped") element types are accepted.

setElementBonePosition.description: This function sets the position of a bone to the specified coordinates. Currently the [Player](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Player "Element/Player") and [Ped](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Ped "Element/Ped") element types are accepted.

setElementBoneRotation.description: This function sets the rotation of a specific bone relative to the element. Currently the [Player](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Player "Element/Player") and [Ped](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Ped "Element/Ped") element types are accepted.

setElementBoneQuaternion.description:
This function determines how a particular bone rotates in relation to the element.  
The use of [quaternions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quaternion) are more effective and do not generate issues like gimbal lock that might arise with [Euler angles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_angles), so they are a preferable choice for rotation.

setElementCollidableWith.description:
This function can be used to set an element to collide with another element. An element with collisions disabled does not interact physically with the other element.  
**Note:** You can only use this function with the element types listed below.

setElementStreamable.description: This function can be used to disable streaming for an element. This will make sure the element is not virtualized (streamed out from GTA) when the player moves far away from it. This function only works in elements with a physical representation in the world (entities), such as [players](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Player "Player"), [peds](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Ped "Ped"), [vehicles](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Vehicle "Vehicle") and [objects](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Object "Object").

updateElementRpHAnim.description: This function updates GTA bone animation for a given [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element"). Currently the [Player](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Player "Element/Player") and [Ped](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Ped "Element/Ped") element types are accepted. It must be called after [setElementBoneRotation](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/SetElementBoneRotation "SetElementBoneRotation") for changes to take effect. It should only be called once per frame, after you are done rotating bones on that element, as it is quite heavy.

attachElements.description: This function attaches one element to another, so that the first one follows the second whenever it moves. If an attempt is made to attach two elements that are already attached the opposite way (eg theElement becomes theAttachToElement and vice versa), the 1st attachment order is automatically detached in favor of the 2nd attachment order. For example, if carA was attached to carB, now carB is attached to carA. Also, an element cannot be attached to two separate elements at one time. For example, two cars can be attached to one single car, but one single car cannot be attached to two separate cars. If you attempt to do this, the existing attachment will automatically be dropped in favor of the new attachment. For example, if carA is asked to attached to carB then carC, it is only attached to carC. This is not compatible with all elements. The following elements are compatible:

createElement.description: This function is used to create a new dummy element in the [element tree](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element_tree "Element tree") which do not necessarily represent an entity within the San Andreas world. A common use for this function is for creating custom elements, such as a Flag or a Base. Elements created using this function are placed in the element tree with their parent as the 'dynamic' map element.

destroyElement.description: This function destroys an [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element") and all elements within it in the hierarchy (its children, the children of those children etc). [Player](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Player "Player") elements cannot be destroyed using this function. A player can only be removed from the hierarchy when they quit or are kicked. The root element also cannot be destroyed, however, passing the root as an argument will wipe all elements from the server, except for the players and clients, which will become direct descendants of the root node, and other elements that cannot be destroyed, such as resource root elements. Players are not the only elements that cannot be deleted. This list also includes remote clients and console elements.

detachElements.description: This function detaches attached elements from one another.

getAttachedElements.description: This function returns a table of all the elements attached to the specified element

getElementAlpha.description: This function returns the alpha (transparency) value for the specified [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element"). This can be a [player](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Player "Player"), [ped](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Ped "Ped"), [object](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Object "Object"), [vehicle](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Vehicle "Vehicle") or [weapon](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Weapon "Element/Weapon").

getElementAttachedOffsets.description: This function returns the offsets of an element that has been attached to another element using [attachElements](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/AttachElements "AttachElements").

getElementAttachedTo.description: This function determines the element that the specified element is attached to.

getElementByIndex.description: This function returns an element of the specified type with the specified index.

getElementByID.description: This function returns an element from the specified ID. If more than one element with the same ID exists, only the first one in the order it appears in the XML tree will be returned by this function.

getElementChild.description: This function returns one of the child elements of a given parent element. The child element is selected by its index (0 for the first child, 1 for the second and so on).

getElementChildren.description: This function is used to retrieve a list of the child elements of a given parent element. Note that it will only return direct children and not elements that are further down the [element tree](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element_tree "Element tree").

getElementChildrenCount.description: This function returns the number of children an element has. Note that only the direct children are counted and not elements that are further down the [element tree](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element_tree "Element tree").

getElementCollisionsEnabled.description: This function indicates if a specific element is set to have collisions disabled. An element without collisions does not interact with the physical environment and remains static.

getElementColShape.description: Some elements have an associated colshape, for example [Marker](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Marker "Marker") and [Pickup](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Pickup "Pickup"). This function is used to get the associated colshape.

getElementData.description: This function retrieves [element data](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element_data "Element data") attached to an element under a certain key.

getAllElementData.description: Returns a table of all element data of an element.

hasElementData.description: This function checks if an element has [element data](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element_data "Element data") available under a certain key.

getElementDimension.description: This function allows you to retrieve the dimension of an element. See [Dimension](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Dimension "Dimension") for the list of valid element types. The dimension determines what/who the element is visible to.

getElementHealth.description: This function returns the current health for the specified [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element"). This can be a [player](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Player "Player"), a [ped](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Ped "Ped"), a [vehicle](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Vehicle "Vehicle"), or an [object](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Object "Object").

getElementID.description: This function gets the ID of an element. This is the "id" attribute of the element and is a string, NOT a number like a model ID, weapons ID or similar.

getElementInterior.description: This function allows you to retrieve the interior of any element. An interior is the current loaded place, 0 being outside.

getElementMatrix.description: This function gets an [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element")'s transform [matrix](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Matrix "Matrix"). This contains 16 float values that multiplied to a point will give you the point transformed. It is most useful for matrix calculations such as calculating offsets. For further information, please refer to a tutorial of matrices in computer graphics programming.

getElementModel.description: Returns the model ID of a given element. This can be a player/ped skin, a pickup model, an object model or a vehicle model.

getElementParent.description: This function is used to determine the parent of an _element_.

getElementPosition.description: The getElementPosition function allows you to retrieve the position coordinates of an element. This can be any real world element, including:

getElementsByType.description: This function is used to retrieve a list of all elements of the specified type. This can be useful, as it disregards _where_ in the element tree it is. It can be used with either the built in types (listed below) or with any custom type used in a .map file. For example, if there is an element of type "flag" (e.g. <flag />) in the .map file, the using "flag" as the type argument would find it.

getElementsWithinColShape.description: This function is used to retrieve a list of all elements in a colshape, of the specified type.

getElementsWithinRange.description: This function is used to retrieve a list of all elements of specified type within a range of 3D coordinates.

getElementType.description: This function is used to retrieve the type of an element.

getLowLODElement.description: This function return the low LOD element that an element is associated with.

getRootElement.description: This function returns the root node of the [element tree](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element_tree "Element tree"), called _root_. This node contains every other element: all resource root elements, players and remote clients. It is never destroyed and cannot be destroyed using [destroyElement](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DestroyElement "DestroyElement"). It is often used to attach handler functions to events triggered for any element, or also to make a scripting function affect all elements.

isElement.description: This function checks if a value is an [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element") or not.

isElementAttached.description: This functions checks whether or not an element is attached to another element.

isElementCallPropagationEnabled.description: This functions checks if certain element has call propagation enabled.

isElementDoubleSided.description: This function checks whether an element is double-sided as set by [setElementDoubleSided](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/SetElementDoubleSided "SetElementDoubleSided") or not.

isElementFrozen.description: This function checks if element has been frozen.

isElementInWater.description: This function checks whether an [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element") is submerged in water.

isElementLowLOD.description: This function reveals if an element is low LOD.

isElementWithinColShape.description: This function is used to determine if an element is within a collision shape. Please note that for legacy reasons, a colshape created on the client does not collide with elements already existing at that location until they first move. Please also note that before 1.0.3, this did not function correctly when moving a colshape. Please note that this function doesn't verify whether element is in the same dimension and interior, additional checks could be implemented manually if they are needed.

isElementWithinMarker.description: This function is used to determine if an [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element") is within a [marker](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Marker "Marker").

setElementAlpha.description: This function sets the alpha (transparency) value for the specified [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element"). This can be a [player](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Player "Player"), [ped](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Ped "Ped"), [object](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Object "Object"), [vehicle](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Vehicle "Vehicle") or [weapon](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Weapon "Element/Weapon").

setElementAngularVelocity.description: Sets the angular velocity of a specified, supported element (Applies a spin to it).

getElementAngularVelocity.description: Gets the current angular velocity of a specified, supported element.

setElementAttachedOffsets.description: This function updates the offsets of an element that has been attached to another element using [attachElements](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/AttachElements "AttachElements").

setElementCallPropagationEnabled.description: This function enables/disables call propagation on a certain element. Look at the example for a practical application.

setElementCollisionsEnabled.description: This function can disable or enable an element's collisions. An element without collisions does not interact with the physical environment and remains static.

setElementData.description:
This function stores [element data](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element_data "Element data") under a certain key, attached to an element. Element data set using this is then synced with all clients and the server. The data can contain server-created elements, but you should avoid passing data that is not able to be synced such as xmlnodes, acls, aclgroups etc. As element data is synced to all clients, it can generate a lot of network traffic and be heavy on performance. Events are much more efficient for sending data from a client to the server only, or from the server to a specific client.  
Usage of element data should be discouraged where your goal can be achieved with events like above, and [tables](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Table "Table") for storing and retrieving data. Note this mode only works when setting element data serverside. Setting data clientside still sends the update to all clients if 'synchronize' is set to true.

setElementDimension.description: This function allows you to set the [dimension](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Dimension "Dimension") of an element. See [Dimension](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Dimension "Dimension") for the in-depth explanation and the list of valid element types.

setElementDoubleSided.description: This function allows you to set the double-sidedness of an element's model. When an element's model is double-sided, it's back facing triangles become visible. Possible uses of double-sidedness are: Elimination of invisible walls, using buildings as enclosures, using inverted landmasses as large pits or to make cave networks. It can also remove the need to add extra triangles to custom models when trying to make them appear solid from all directions.

setElementFrozen.description: This function freezes an element (stops it in its position and disables movement) or unfreezes it.

setElementHealth.description: This function sets the health for the specified [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element"). This can be a [ped](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Ped "Ped"), [object](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Object "Object") or a [vehicle](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Vehicle "Vehicle").

setElementID.description: This function sets the ID of an element to a string. This can be anything from an identifying number, to a name. You can only change the ID of an element clientside if that element has been created clientside as well.

setElementInterior.description: This function allows you to set the [interior](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Interior "Interior") of any element. An interior is the current loaded place, 0 being outside.

setElementModel.description: Sets the model of a given element. This allows you to change the model of a player (or ped), a vehicle or an object.

setElementParent.description: This function is used for setting an element as the parent of another element.

setElementPosition.description: This function sets the position of an element to the specified coordinates.

setElementRotation.description: Sets the rotation of elements according to the world (does not work with players that are on the ground).

setElementVelocity.description: This function sets the velocity (movement speeds) along each axis, for an element. This is not compatible with all elements. Only the following element types are compatible:

setLowLODElement.description: This function assigns a low LOD element to an element. The low LOD element is displayed when its associated element is not fully visible. If a low LOD element is assigned to several elements, it will be displayed when any of these elements are not fully visible.

getPedContactElement.description: This function detects the element a ped is standing on. This can be a vehicle or an object.

getResourceDynamicElementRoot.description: This function retrieves the _dynamic element root_ of a specified [resource](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Resource "Resource"). The _dynamic element root_ is the parent of elements that are created by scripts (e.g. with [createObject](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/CreateObject "CreateObject")) unless they specify a different parent.

getResourceRootElement.description: This function retrieves a resource's root element. The resource's root element is the element in the element tree which is the parent of all elements that belong to a particular resource (except for elements specifically created elsewhere). You can attach event handlers to this element to easily capture events that originate from your resource (and global events that originate from the root element). Note: every resource has a [predefined global variable](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Predefined_variables_list "Predefined variables list") called _resourceRoot_ whose value is the root element of that resource.

engineApplyShaderToWorldTexture.description: This function applies a [shader](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Shader "Shader") to one or more world textures.

engineFreeModel.description: This function is used to un-assign the specified model ID from the [engineRequestModel](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/EngineRequestModel "EngineRequestModel") assignment.

engineGetModelIDFromName.description: This function gets the model ID of an object model from object name. This function is the counterpart of [engineGetModelNameFromID](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/EngineGetModelNameFromID "EngineGetModelNameFromID").

engineGetModelLODDistance.description: This function gets the LOD distance for any object / model ID.

engineGetModelNameFromID.description: This function gets the model name of an object model from model ID. This function is the counterpart of [engineGetModelIDFromName](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/EngineGetModelIDFromName "EngineGetModelIDFromName").

engineGetModelPhysicalPropertiesGroup.description: This function gets physical properties group id used by given model.

engineGetModelTextureNames.description: This function returns a table of the world textures which are applied to the specified model.

engineGetModelTextures.description: This function allows you to get the textures of any model.

engineGetModelVisibleTime.description: This function returns a model's visibility time, this is used for example for building lights being shown after 23:00.

engineGetObjectGroupPhysicalProperty.description: This function gets physical property of given properties group.

engineGetSurfaceProperties.description: This function retrieves the value of a surface property.

engineGetVisibleTextureNames.description: This function returns a list of the world textures which are being used to draw the current scene.

engineImageGetFilesCount.description: This function returns the number of files an IMG file has.

engineImportTXD.description: This function imports (adds) a loaded RenderWare Texture Dictionary into a specific model. This is necessary in order for the DFF loader to find any new textures. Please **call this function before loading the DFF model file**, in order to allow the DFF loading process to find the new textures. This function can also replace default GTA textures, so that it becomes possible to e.g. put custom images on existing billboards. Ped and weapon textures are also supported. CJ clothing component textures can be replaced by using the ids listed on [this page](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Clothing_Component_IDs "Clothing Component IDs").

engineLoadCOL.description: This function loads a RenderWare Collision (COL 1/2/3) file into GTA. The collisions can then be used to provide collisions for in-game objects. For vehicles, please omit this function by embedding your [COL](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/COL "COL") file into your [DFF](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DFF "DFF") file. This way, you can be sure that the COL file is correctly (and automatically) loaded when calling [engineLoadDFF](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/EngineLoadDFF "EngineLoadDFF"). This is a client side function. Be sure to transfer your COL file by including it in the meta file.

engineLoadDFF.description: This function loads a RenderWare Model (DFF) file into GTA. To successfully load your model with textures, be sure to use [engineLoadTXD](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/EngineLoadTXD "EngineLoadTXD") and [engineImportTXD](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/EngineImportTXD "EngineImportTXD") before calling this function. If some error occurs while loading the DFF, MTA will output a message - check out [DFF error messages](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DFF_error_messages "DFF error messages") to know what they mean. This is a client side function. Be sure to transfer your DFF file by including it in the meta file. The returned [DFF](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DFF "DFF") element is an element in the element tree, just like vehicles and objects. When the dff is destroyed, ie on resource unload or using [destroyElement](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DestroyElement "DestroyElement"), any elements that use the DFF, such as vehicles or objects will be reset.

engineLoadIMG.description: If you're experiencing crashes/game hangs with default values, try to adjust memory/buffer/cache sizes with [engineStreamingSetMemorySize](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/EngineStreamingSetMemorySize "EngineStreamingSetMemorySize"), [engineStreamingSetBufferSize](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/EngineStreamingSetBufferSize "EngineStreamingSetBufferSize") and/or [engineStreamingSetModelCacheLimits](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/EngineStreamingSetModelCacheLimits "EngineStreamingSetModelCacheLimits").

engineLoadIFP.description: This function loads an animation library (IFP) file into GTA with a custom block name. All three IFP formats are supported ANPK, ANP2, and ANP3. Unfortunately, GTA 3 animations are not supported, however, you can load GTA:VC IFP files using this function. You don't have to replace any animation to play a custom one, to play a custom animation, load the IFP file using this function, then use [setPedAnimation](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/SetPedAnimation "SetPedAnimation"). If you wish to replace a GTA internal animation with a custom one, you can use [engineReplaceAnimation](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/EngineReplaceAnimation "EngineReplaceAnimation"). To unload the IFP file, use [destroyElement](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/DestroyElement "DestroyElement"), restarting or stopping the resource can also unload the IFP file automatically.

engineLoadTXD.description: This function loads a RenderWare Texture Dictionary (TXD) file into GTA. The texture dictionary can then be used to provide textures. This is a client side function. Be sure to transfer your TXD file by including it in the meta file.

engineRemoveShaderFromWorldTexture.description: This function removes a [shader](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Shader "Shader") from one or more world textures.

engineReplaceAnimation.description: This function replaces a specific internal (default) animation with a custom one that has been loaded using [engineLoadIFP](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/EngineLoadIFP "EngineLoadIFP") function. This function only affects a specific [player](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Player "Player") or [ped](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Ped "Ped"), the [internal animation](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Animations "Animations") is not replaced for everyone, for instance, different players and peds are able to have completely different crouching, walking, and fighting etc., animations running simultaneously at the same time. Also, it's not synchronized, you'll need to execute this function on every client in Lua to synchronize it. Internal animations replaced using this function can still be played with [setPedAnimation](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/SetPedAnimation "SetPedAnimation"). You can restore replaced animations back with [engineRestoreAnimation](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/EngineRestoreAnimation "EngineRestoreAnimation"). It should be noted that partial animations are not supported, you can still replace them, but they won't work as intended, for example, "FightA\_block" animation from "ped" block is a partial animation, you can't replace it properly, only a few animations are partial, rest of them are not, so it shouldn't be a problem.

engineReplaceCOL.description: This function replaces the collision file of the given model id to the collision file passed. Use [engineLoadCOL](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/EngineLoadCOL "EngineLoadCOL") to load the collision file first.

engineReplaceModel.description: This function replaces the given model ID with the model contained in a DFF file loaded by [engineLoadDFF](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/EngineLoadDFF "EngineLoadDFF"). This function supports [vehicles](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Vehicle "Vehicle"), [objects](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Object "Object"), [peds](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Ped "Ped") and [players](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Player "Player") but not CJ clothing and body parts. To replace weapon models you must use their object IDs, not weapon IDs. There is a weapon model list available at [weapons](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Weapons "Weapons").

engineRequestModel.description: This function is used to assign the next available model ID to a certain element type.

engineResetModelLODDistance.description: This function resets the LOD distance for an object / model ID.

engineResetSurfaceProperties.description: This function resets a surface property to its default value. If no ID is provided, it will reset all surfaces' properties to their original values.

engineRestoreAnimation.description: This function restores internal (default) animations that were replaced using [engineReplaceAnimation](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/EngineReplaceAnimation "EngineReplaceAnimation") function. This function only affects a specific [player](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Player "Player") or [ped](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Ped "Ped") just like [engineReplaceAnimation](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/EngineReplaceAnimation "EngineReplaceAnimation"). If only 1st parameter ([ped](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Ped "Ped")) is provided to this function, all replaced animations are restored. If block name is also provided for 2nd parameter, then replaced animations within that block are restored. If 3rd parameter (animation name) is provided, then only that specific animation within that specific block is restored.

engineRestoreCOL.description: This function restores the original collision model of the given model ID. Reverses the effect of [engineReplaceCOL](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/EngineReplaceCOL "EngineReplaceCOL").

engineRestoreModel.description: This function restores the visual DFF model of the given model ID. This restores the result of [engineReplaceModel](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/EngineReplaceModel "EngineReplaceModel").

engineRestoreModelPhysicalPropertiesGrou.description: This function restores original physical properties group used by given model.

engineRestoreObjectGroupPhysicalProperti.description: This function restores all physical properties of given properties group.

engineRestreamWorld.description: This function re-streams everything in the GTA world. Read [this pull request](https://github.com/multitheftauto/mtasa-blue/pull/1735) to understand what it is for.

engineSetAsynchronousLoading.description: This function enables or disables asynchronous model loading. Enabling asynchronous model loading may reduce the small pauses that occur when a new model is displayed for the first time. However, it can cause the new models to appear slightly later than they might have otherwise.

engineSetModelLODDistance.description:
This function sets a custom LOD distance for any object / model ID. This is the distance at which objects of that model ID are switched to their LOD model, or (if there is no LOD model) become invisible. **Notes:** The actual draw distance used is modified by the draw distance slider in the settings 'Video' tab of the MTA client. However, there is a general draw distance limit of 300 units. So engineSetModelLODDistance(1337,400) will mean model 1337 will be visible up to a distance of 300 units no matter what the 'Video' tab says. Therefore, unless it's really important, engineSetModelLODDistance should not be set to anything greater than 170.  
170 will still give the maximum draw distance (of 300 units) on clients that have a 'Video' tab draw distance setting of 100%, and it will help reduce lag for players who chose a lower draw distance in their settings. For low LOD elements, engineSetModelLODDistance still has a limit of 300 units, but the actual draw distance used is 5 times the setting value. Also, low LOD elements ignore the 'Video' tab draw distance slider. So a setting of 200 will mean a low LOD element will always have a draw distance of **1000** units.

engineSetModelPhysicalPropertiesGroup.description: This function sets physical properties group id used by given model.

engineSetModelVisibleTime.description: This function changes model visibility time, this is used for example for building lights being shown after 23:00.

engineSetObjectGroupPhysicalProperty.description: This function sets physical property of given properties group.

engineSetSurfaceProperties.description: This function changes a property of a surface.

engineStreamingFreeUpMemory.description: This function frees up the streaming RAM memory.

engineStreamingGetUsedMemory.description: This function gets the amount of memory (in bytes) used by the GTA streamer.

engineStreamingSetMemorySize.description: Restores the maximum amount of RAM \[in bytes\] that can be used for streaming to the default value

engineStreamingGetMemorySize.description: Gets the maximum amount of RAM \[in bytes\] that can be used for streaming

engineStreamingSetBufferSize.description: Set the streaming buffer size. The larger it is, the more models can be loaded in one go BUT increases the RAM \[**not** streaming memory!\] usage. Can help with custom IMG loading speed by reducing pop-in.

engineStreamingGetBufferSize.description: Get the streaming buffer size \[**not** maximum memory size\]

engineStreamingRestoreBufferSize.description: This function resets the streaming buffer. The value is automatically reset when disconnected.

engineStreamingSetModelCacheLimits.description: This function sets custom cache limits for vehicle and pedestrian models based on provided values. The arguments that receive zero mean complete deactivation.

triggerLatentServerEvent.description: This function is the same as [triggerServerEvent](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/TriggerServerEvent "TriggerServerEvent") except the transmission rate of the data contained in the arguments can be limited and other network traffic is not blocked while the data is being transferred.

triggerServerEvent.description: This function triggers an event previously registered on the server. This is the primary means of passing information between the client and the server. Servers have a similar [triggerClientEvent](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/TriggerClientEvent "TriggerClientEvent") function that can do the reverse. You can treat this function as if it was an asynchronous function call, using [triggerClientEvent](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/TriggerClientEvent "TriggerClientEvent") to pass back any returned information if necessary. Almost any data types can be passed as expected, including [elements](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element") and complex nested [tables](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Table "Table"). Non-element MTA data types like xmlNodes or resource pointers will not be able to be passed as they do not necessarily have a valid representation on the client. **Elements of the Vector or Matrix classes cannot be passed!** Events are sent reliably, so the server will receive them, but there may be (but shouldn't be) a significant delay before they are received. You should take this into account when using them. Keep in mind the bandwidth issues when using events - don't pass a large list of arguments unless you really need to. **It is marginally more efficient to pass one large event than two smaller ones**.

addEvent.description: This function allows you to register a custom [event](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Event "Event"). Custom events function exactly like the built-in events. See [event system](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Event_system "Event system") for more information on the event system.

addEventHandler.description: This function will add an [event](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Event "Event") handler. An event handler is a function that will be called when the event it's attached to is triggered. See [event system](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Event_system "Event system") for more information on how the event system works. Event handlers are functions that are called when a particular event happens. Each event specifies a specific set of variables that are passed to the event handler and can be read by your function. The following global variables are available for use in handler functions: It is important to remember that events pass up and down the [element tree](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element_tree "Element tree"). An event triggered on the root element is triggered on every element in the tree. An event triggered on any other element is triggered on its ancestors (its parent element and its parent's parent etc) and its children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren. You can use the _propagate_ argument to specify if you wish your handler to receive events that have propagated up or down the tree. The order in which event handlers are triggered is undefined, you should not rely on one event handler being executed before another. Each function closure can only be added once to each event. On the second attempt to add the function closure to the same event a warning will be emitted to the debug console and the call to addEventHandler will fail.

cancelEvent.description: This function is used to stop the automatic internal handling of events, for example this can be used to prevent an item being given to a player when they walk over a pickup, by canceling the [onPickupUse](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/OnPickupUse "OnPickupUse") event. cancelEvent does not have an effect on all events, see the individual event's pages for information on what happens when the event is canceled. cancelEvent does not stop further event handlers from being called, as the order of event handlers being called is undefined in many cases. Instead, you can see if the currently active event has been cancelled using [wasEventCancelled](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/WasEventCancelled "WasEventCancelled"). The use of cancelEvent outside of an event handler has no effect. If you implement your own custom events and want to handle them being cancelled, you should call [wasEventCancelled](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/WasEventCancelled "WasEventCancelled") to check after your call to [triggerEvent](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/TriggerEvent "TriggerEvent").

cancelLatentEvent.description: Stops a latent event from completing

getEventHandlers.description: This function gets the attached functions from the event and attached element from current lua script.

getLatentEventHandles.description: Gets the currently queued latent events. The last one in the table is always the latest event queued. Each returned handle can be used with [getLatentEventStatus](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/GetLatentEventStatus "GetLatentEventStatus") or [cancelLatentEvent](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/CancelLatentEvent "CancelLatentEvent")

getLatentEventStatus.description: Gets the status of one queued latent event.

removeEventHandler.description: This functions removes a handler function from an [event](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Event "Event"), so that the function is not called anymore when the event is triggered. See [event system](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Event_system "Event system") for more information on how the event system works.

triggerEvent.description: This function will trigger a named [event](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Event "Event") on a specific [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element") in the [element tree](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element_tree "Element tree"). See [event system](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Event_system "Event system") for more information on how the event system works. You can use the value returned from this function to determine if the event was cancelled by one of the event handlers. You should determine what your response (if any) to this should be based on the event's purpose. Generally, cancelling an event should prevent any further code being run that is dependent on whatever triggered that event. For example, if you have an _onFlagCapture_ event, cancelling it would be expected to prevent the flag being able to be captured. Similarly, if you have _onPlayerKill_ as an event you trigger, canceling it would either be expected to prevent the player being killed from dying or at least prevent the player from getting a score for it.

wasEventCancelled.description: This function checks if the last completed event was cancelled. This is mainly useful for custom events created by scripts.
