Events can be cancelled using [cancelEvent](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/CancelEvent "CancelEvent"), this indicates that the resource which triggered the event should do whatever it can to reverse any changes made by whatever caused the event. See [triggerEvent](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/TriggerEvent "TriggerEvent") for a more detailed explanation of this.

createFire.description: Creates a patch of fire that will spread a bit and die out after a while. Because it's a client side only function, other players won't see it, so custom events or custom objects will be needed to make a fire visible to some players.

extinguishFire.description: This function is used to extinguish all spreading fire, or spreading fire at specified coordinates.

getAnalogControlState.description: This retrieves the analog control state of a control. This is useful for detecting sensitive controls, such as those used on a joypad. To get the analog control state for a [ped](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Ped "Ped"), please use [getPedAnalogControlState](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/GetPedAnalogControlState "GetPedAnalogControlState").

getBoundKeys.description: Returns a list of key names that are bound to the specified game [control](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Control_names "Control names") or console command.

getCommandsBoundToKey.description: Gets the commands bound to a key.

getKeyBoundToCommand.description: This function allow you get first key bound to command.

getKeyState.description: This function determines if a certain key is pressed or not. **Note:** 'ralt' may trigger both 'ralt' and 'lctrl', this is due to AltGr

setAnalogControlState.description: This sets the analog control state of a control for the local player. To change the analog controls for a [ped](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Ped "Ped"), please use [setPedAnalogControlState](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/SetPedAnalogControlState "SetPedAnalogControlState").

addCommandHandler.description: This function will attach a scripting function (handler) to a console command, so that whenever a player or administrator uses the command the function is called. Multiple command handlers can be attached to a single command, and they will be called in the order that the handlers were attached. Equally, multiple commands can be handled by a single function, and the _commandName_ parameter used to decide the course of action. For users, a command is in the format: _commandName_ _argument1_ _argument2_ This can be triggered from the player's console or directly from the chat box by prefixing the message with a forward slash (_/_). For server side handlers, the server admin is also able to trigger these directly from the server's console in the same way as they are triggered from a player's console.

bindKey.description: Binds a player's key to a handler function or command, which will be called when the key is pressed.

executeCommandHandler.description: This function will call all the attached functions of an existing console command, for a specified player.

getCommandHandlers.description: This function is used to retrieve a list of all the registered command handlers of a given resource (or of all resources). Function also added client-side.

getFunctionsBoundToKey.description: Gets the functions bound to a key. To bind a function to a key use the [bindKey](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/BindKey "BindKey") function

getKeyBoundToFunction.description: getKeyBoundToFunction allows retrieval of the first key bound to a function.

isControlEnabled.description: Checks whether a GTA control is enabled or disabled for a certain player.

removeCommandHandler.description: This function removes a command handler, that is one that has been added using [addCommandHandler](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/AddCommandHandler "AddCommandHandler"). This function can only remove command handlers that were added by the resource that it is called in.

toggleAllControls.description: Enables or disables the use of all GTA controls for a specified player.

toggleControl.description: Enables or disables the use of a GTA control for a specific player.

unbindKey.description: Removes an existing key bind from the specified player.

createLight.description: This function creates a 3D [light](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Light "Element/Light") in the world.

getLightColor.description: This function returns the color for a [light](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Light "Element/Light") element.

getLightDirection.description: This function returns the direction for a [light](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Light "Element/Light") element.

getLightRadius.description: This function returns the radius for a [light](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Light "Element/Light") element.

getLightType.description: This function returns the type for a [light](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Light "Element/Light") element.

setLightColor.description: This function sets the color for a [light](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Light "Element/Light") element.

setLightDirection.description: This function sets the direction for a [light](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Light "Element/Light") element.

setLightRadius.description: This function sets the radius for a [light](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element/Light "Element/Light") element.

isCoronaReflectionEnabled.description: This function gets visibility of corona reflection.

setCoronaReflectionEnabled.description: This function sets visibility of corona reflection.

createMarker.description: This function creates a marker. A marker is a 3D model in the world that can highlight a particular point or area, often used to instruct players where to go to perform actions such as entering buildings. There are various limits that govern the maximum number of each type that can be visible at once. These are: You are able to create as many markers as you wish (memory and element limit permitting), but the player will only be able to see the nearest ones up to the limit.

getMarkerColor.description: This function returns the color and transparency for a marker element.

getMarkerCount.description: Returns the number of markers that currently exist in the world.

getMarkerIcon.description: This function returns the icon name for a marker.

getMarkerSize.description: This function returns a [float](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Float "Float") containing the size of the specified marker.

getMarkerType.description: This function returns a marker's type.

setMarkerColor.description: This function sets the color of the specified marker by modifying the values for red, green, blue and alpha.

setMarkerIcon.description: This function allows changing the icon of a checkpoint marker.

setMarkerSize.description: This function sets the size of the specified marker. Setting negative value will "flip" the marker, do nothing or make it invisible:

setMarkerTarget.description: This function sets the 'target' for a marker. Only the _checkpoint_ and _ring_ marker types can have a target. For _checkpoint_ markers, the target is shown as an arrow aiming at the point specified. Only 5 arrows can be visible at the same time. For _ring_ markers, the target is shown by rotating the whole ring so that it faces the point specified. This function is most useful for setting up markers for races, where each marker points to the next one's position. (This is mostly used in races!)

setMarkerType.description: This function changes a marker's type. The type controls how the marker is displayed in the game. It's important that you use marker types that users are used to from the single player game. For example, checkpoints are used in races, rings are used for aircraft races, arrows are used for entering buildings etc.

createObject.description: Creates an [object](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Object "Object") [element](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Element "Element") at a given position and rotation.

breakObject.description: This function breaks a specific object.

getObjectScale.description: This function returns the visible size of an object.

moveObject.description: This function will smoothly move an object from its current position to a specified rotation and position.

respawnObject.description: This function respawns a specific object.

toggleObjectRespawn.description: This function is used to toggle if an object should respawn after it got destroyed

setObjectScale.description: This function changes the visible size of an object.

isObjectMoving.description: This function checks if an [object](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Object "Object") is moving.

isObjectBreakable.description: This function checks if an object / model ID is breakable.

setObjectBreakable.description: This function sets an object to be breakable/unbreakable.

stopObject.description: This will allow you to stop an object that is currently moving.

getObjectMass.description: This function returns the mass of a specified object.

getObjectProperty.description: This function gets a property of the specified [object](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Object "Object").

setObjectMass.description: This function sets the mass of a specified object. Changing the mass leads to a different movement behavior for especially dynamic objects.

setObjectProperty.description: This function sets a property of the specified [object](https://wiki.multitheftauto.com/wiki/Object "Object").

clearDebugBox.description: This function clears the debug box.

isChatInputBlocked.description: This function checks if the player's chat input is blocked.

isChatVisible.description: This function checks if player's chat is visible.

clearChatBox.description: This function clears the chatbox. It does not clear the console (F8)
